The observed high heldout error in the rigid family experiments is not due to the function space complexity, but rather a transport bottleneck where the optimization landscape (L-BFGS-B) fails to converge to the global minimum due to poor conditioning of the Hessian near the linear manifold, requiring adaptive learning rate schedules or preconditioning rather than increased network capacity.
